name: search_first_catan_v15_human_finish_guard
description: Search-first base-Catan strategy: use Catanatron AlphaBeta depth-2 as the primary move source, with Codex guardrails for expansion quality, finish/threat play, human-leader defense, Longest Road defense, stricter settlement reserve before final city upgrades, and safe robber moves.
notes: This is a reset from the old city-first strategy. Do not force ore/wheat if the map gives no expansion tempo.
Opening goal: the two starting settlements together should cover at least four resource types and ideally all five. Missing wood+brick is dangerous because it blocks expansion.
Second opening settlement must complement the first. If the first settlement lacks brick or sheep, the second must strongly prefer adding those resources over duplicating wheat/ore/wood.

After the opening settlements are placed, evaluate expansion nodes by marginal production, missing resources, ports, and route cost. Do not reject a midgame settlement just because the single node itself does not cover four resource types.

Pick a coherent opening archetype from the board: expansion/road if wood+brick are strong, city/dev if ore+wheat+sheep are strong, hybrid if both are available. Never optimize only one settlement in isolation.
Strong numbers matter, but resource coverage and build plans matter more than a high-pip dead resource pile.
Ports are support tools, not the whole plan. Value 3:1 and matching-resource ports when they convert repeated surplus into missing build resources.
Build settlements early when legal; more production and more resource coverage beat passing while waiting for a perfect city.
Build cities when affordable, especially on high-production wheat/ore/sheep. A city is normally better than an extra road because it gives immediate VP and doubles production.

After two cities, if the bot has fewer than four total buildings or zero live settlements, switch back to expansion pressure: trade for road/settlement resources and open new settlement spots before buying more development cards.

Buy development cards when city/settlement is unavailable and the hand can support ore+wheat+sheep, but do not spam them. After Largest Army or 4-5 total dev cards, prioritize visible VP from settlements/cities.
Do not buy another development card while holding an unplayed tactical development card such as Knight, Year of Plenty, Monopoly, or Road Building. Convert the existing card into tempo first.
Play Year of Plenty when it immediately completes a city, settlement, or development-card plan; otherwise avoid adding cards just to make the hand larger.

Use maritime trade aggressively when stuck or above seven cards: surplus resources above keep-targets should become missing settlement, city, or development-card resources before ending the turn. Do not spend repeated 4:1 trades just to extend a road chain.

Hand pressure rule: ending a turn with more than seven resources is usually a mistake. Before END_TURN, accept imperfect maritime trades, buy a development card, or build a useful road if that reduces discard exposure.

Roads must point toward a reachable settlement, port, or longest-road plan. Intermediate roads are useful when they shorten a route to a high-value legal settlement node within the route lookahead window; do not build roads just to dump two cards.
Before building an expansion road, score whether an opponent can claim the same settlement node sooner or with fewer missing resources. Penalize contested routes instead of racing blindly.

After the two opening settlements and roads, do not build another road unless it directly opens a legal settlement target and the hand is at most one resource short of building that settlement. If not, wait/trade/build city or development card instead.

Track road debt: if road count is high relative to settlements plus cities, stop extending routes unless the next road makes a settlement nearly buildable or the game is at 8+ VP and Longest Road can immediately swing the result.
After three total buildings, transition toward cities. Do not keep building road chains while sitting on zero or one city unless the expansion settlement is one resource away.
Two-hex coastal settlement spots can be correct, especially with a useful port, missing resource, or strong number pair. Do not require every expansion target to touch three land hexes.

A road endpoint is not enough by itself: prefer roads that improve the shortest path to a legal settlement candidate under distance-2 rules. Roads around existing cities/settlements are fake progress unless they unlock a concrete expansion route.
Road Building is enabled only when it supports Longest Road defense or an immediate road-race plan; normal random route dumping is still blocked.
Before ending a turn with more than seven cards, prefer any useful build, targeted trade, or development card to reduce discard exposure.

Endgame rule: at 8+ actual VP, stop optimizing general production. Prefer the shortest route to 10 VP: direct city/settlement, then Longest Road if one road can flip it, then development cards/trades for hidden VP.
At 8+ VP, if all settlements have already become cities, rebuild a live settlement route instead of passing with only city/development-card plans.
High-score maritime trades under discard pressure may exceed the normal soft cap, but only within the stricter override cap.
Use Catanatron AlphaBeta depth-2 as the primary decision source. Codex strategy is now a guardrail layer, not the main policy.
Use Catanatron's one-ply base value-function teacher only as a fallback correction when full search is unavailable. The teacher must not override END_TURN into a weak road or a capped maritime trade.
When all settlement/city pieces are exhausted, maritime trades should no longer target those plans. Convert surplus into development-card attempts or Longest Road only.
Robber should block the leader/highest-production opponent tile while avoiding self-blocking.
Post-search guardrails should reject dead roads and road-debt roads, but still allow roads that move Codex toward a concrete settlement route.
Use development cards more actively when a leader is close to Largest Army; buying and playing knights is part of defense, not only a fallback.
The current live target is a less road-heavy style even if raw self-play win-rate is slightly below the road-heavy v10 profile.

At 8+ VP, switch from general expansion to finish mode: take immediate city/settlement VP and trade only into direct VP plans. Keep normal expansion roads alive at 8 VP, then tighten roads and development-card outs at 9+ VP.
When an opponent has 8+ public VP or a visible road/army swing, treat defense as urgent. Prefer knight/dev-card control over non-final roads or generic trades.
v14 adds Longest Road defense earlier than the pure finish race: when an opponent has a credible road lead, allow road contest/denial if the gap stays close and the road is not dead.
v14 preserves the last live settlement before a city upgrade unless the city wins immediately or Codex still has a reachable settlement route with enough resources to rebuild expansion.
v14 opening evaluation treats weak single-number resource coverage as unreliable, especially for wood/brick expansion resources and ore/wheat city resources.
v15 makes the second opening settlement pay a large penalty for still missing wood or brick, because high-pip ore/wheat starts without expansion tempo collapsed in live human games.

v15 city reserve evaluates the board after the city build. At 8+ VP, a city that leaves Codex with zero or one live settlement is blocked unless a concrete settlement route remains close after spending the city resources.
v15 treats a human leader as urgent earlier than a Catanatron leader: 7 public VP, 8 effective VP, a visible road race, or one played knight can activate shutdown/defense logic.
v15 protects visible 9-VP settlement routes from being overridden by generic development-card or army-defense buys.
